builds.name: Reference: AP dive
builds.goal: Reference for Fizz: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A melee assassin who punctuates attack-enhanced trades with untargetability and a delayed shark engage. Compare W/attack weaving with spell burst while retaining E escape timing. A Spellblade proc needs an actual compatible attack, and the shark must land at the recorded range. AP, penetration and Rocketbelt access test a short committed damage window.
builds.summary: AP, penetration and Rocketbelt access test a short committed damage window.
testPlan: Kit question for Fizz: Compare W/attack weaving with spell burst while retaining E escape timing. A Spellblade proc needs an actual compatible attack, and the shark must land at the recorded range.

Start with the early core (Rocketbelt, then Shadowflame) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: AP, penetration and Rocketbelt access test a short committed damage window. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Fizz dashes through his target, dealing magic damage and applying on hit effects. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: The active cannot replace every mobility tool; minimal sustained durability.

The route fails Fizz's stated kit question: Compare W/attack weaving with spell burst while retaining E escape timing. A Spellblade proc needs an actual compatible attack, and the shark must land at the recorded range.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: The active cannot replace every mobility tool; minimal sustained durability.
Full cost 16,700 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
The reference is a research control, not a claim of the current highest-win-rate build.
buyOrder: Rocketbelt, then Shadowflame. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff, Zhonya's Hourglass are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

kitEvidence.formula:
Fizz hops onto his trident, becoming Untargetable for 0.75 seconds, after which he deals [80 / 130 / 180 / 230 / 280 + (0.95) × AP] magic damage to nearby enemies and Slows them by [(0.4 / 0.45 / 0.5 / 0.55 / 0.6) × 100]% for [2] seconds. 

Fizz can Recast this Ability while Untargetable to dash again, which ends the effect early, deals damage in a smaller area, and doesn't Slow.
Fizz is Ghosted and takes [4 + (0.01) × AP] reduced damage from all sources.

Passive: Fizz's Attacks cause his enemies to bleed, dealing [30 / 45 / 60 / 75 / 90 + (0.25) × AP] magic damage over [3] seconds. 

Active: Fizz's next Attack deals an additional [50 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 150 + (0.45) × AP] magic damage. If this Attack kills its target, Fizz refunds [30 / 40 / 50 / 60 / 70] Mana and reduces the cooldown of this Ability to [1] second. If it does not kill, Fizz's Attacks deal an additional [20 / 25 / 30 / 35 / 40 + (0.3) × AP] magic damage for [5] seconds.

Fizz launches a fish that attaches to the first champion hit. The victim is afflicted with True Sight and Slowed by between 40% to 80% based on how far the fish travelled before attaching. 

After [2] seconds a shark erupts on the target, Knocking Up the target with the fish for 1 second, Knocking Back everything else, and dealing between [180 / 300 / 420 + (0.6) × AP] to [(180 / 300 / 420 + (0.6) × AP) × (1.5)] magic damage based on how far the fish travelled before attaching.
Fizz dashes through an enemy, dealing [(1) × AD] physical damage plus [10 / 25 / 40 / 55 / 70 + (0.55) × AP] magic damage.

builds.name: Nonlethal Trident Window
builds.summary: Compare W nonlethal follow-up versus W kill/refund sequence.
builds.goal: Compare W nonlethal follow-up versus W kill/refund sequence.
builds.hypothesis: If W's empowered attack fails to kill, it grants five seconds of AP magic damage on subsequent attacks. Nashor/Dusk and Dawn reward this actual attack window, and Q provides access. Cosmic and Riftmaker help stay close while W bleed continues.
testPlan: Required state: First W attack does not kill and target remains reachable for follow-up attacks.
Compare W nonlethal follow-up versus W kill/refund sequence; repeat at equal gold, finite stacks, same ranks and defenses against a moving target.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Evasion needs E, reducing attacks; target death ends the proposed sustained window.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: W kill cooldown refund and nonlethal five-second buff are alternative outcomes.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Dusk and Dawn, Cosmic Drive, Riftmaker, Rabadon's Deathcap, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Flat Reduction Brawler
builds.summary: Compare survival against equal-total small-packet and large-packet damage.
builds.goal: Compare survival against equal-total small-packet and large-packet damage.
builds.hypothesis: P reduces damage by 4 plus 0.01 AP per source. AP from Riftmaker/Deathcap can modestly increase reduction against repeated small packets; health/resists and Unending Despair buy close-combat time. E untargetability avoids a large threat, while W supplies sustained AP magic damage.
testPlan: Required state: Incoming pattern must include repeated small hits; E timed for the large packet.
Compare survival against equal-total small-packet and large-packet damage; repeat at equal gold, finite stacks, same ranks and defenses against a moving target.

Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Reduction is tiny against burst and defense delays enough AP to matter.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Flat passive reduction is not percentage damage immunity.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
